source: cedia commit 4ead389 (Sub-threads: spawn explore or work into a fresh session, archived when done), redone from its parent

edits.why: The agent's commands already run in the OS sandbox, which cannot open another inside it; verify runs outside it, where this test still runs.
#80 on this older tree: under the macOS sandbox a stat of ~/.ssh gives EPERM, so the base's own policy tests failed before the agent changed anything, and agents 'fixed' real() unasked.

prompt:
Implement this change in cedia, the repository you are in (a coding harness in TypeScript on Bun; AGENTS.md and SPEC.md describe it).

<change>
Sub-threads: spawn explore or work into a fresh session, archived when done

The writer gets a spawn tool. The model says what the work is (explore: read-only; work: may edit) and cedia decides how it runs: explore on the swarm model (default beam, free and fast; the code model under zdr), read-only and in parallel; work on the writer's model under the run's policy, sandbox and checks, alone and between two snapshots, so the parent's ledger records its changes and the done gate still wants a check. Only the child's report enters the parent's context. A sub-thread is its own thread with a parent; it archives itself when it succeeds and stays listed when it fails. Children cannot spawn.

--spawn on|off, --swarm <ref>, roles.swarm and spawn in user settings; cedia threads --all, archive and unarchive. The eval runner passes --cedia-arg through and reports handoffs and sub-threads per run.
</change>

The tests in `test/threads.test.ts` and `test/policy.test.ts` were written for this change and say what it must do. Make them pass without changing them, and keep the whole `bun test` suite passing.
